candidates.change_summary: Delete the require statement that enforces the pending flash governance decision asset, amount, and unlock time, allowing withdrawal for arbitrary keys.
Replace the `< block.timestamp` check in the withdraw require with `> block.timestamp`, so withdrawal succeeds only before the unlock time instead of after it.
Replace the amount transfer argument with `0`, leaving the pending decision entry recorded instead of transferring and deleting its amount.
Delete the final `delete pendingFlashDecision[targetContract][msg.sender]` statement, leaving the withdrawn pending decision entry recorded.
Move the `delete pendingFlashDecision[targetContract][msg.sender]` state update to before the external token transfer call.
Weaken the unlockTime precondition from strictly less-than to less-than-or-equal, allowing withdrawal exactly at unlockTime.
Delete the amount > 0 precondition so a pending decision with zero amount no longer blocks withdrawal.
Change the pending-decision asset check to compare against the wrong state field (amount instead of asset), making the asset match always fail and always revert.
Transfer the hardcoded asset parameter instead of the stored pending asset, changing which token is sent.
Delete the final delete of the pending flash decision so the record remains after withdrawal.
Changed the assignment in endConfiguration to set configured to false instead of true.
Delete the require guard in setDAO, allowing DAO to be overwritten after configuration or by any caller.
Replace the DAO assignment with a no-op self-assignment, so the DAO state variable is never updated by setDAO.
Delete the governer cache-clearing statement, leaving a stale governer after setDAO updates DAO.
Replace the DAO assignment with an assignment to a different value expression (dao address zero), so the stored DAO differs from the argument.
